utterances.text: Considering we discussed jurisdiction, I'll show you 1D00-3301. It's a document from the Military Prosecutor's Office attached to the Main Staff of the VRS, which is the counterpart of the highest civilian prosecutor, which is the Republic Prosecutor's Office. It's a document from 1992. It's called: "Guidelines for Identifying Criteria for Criminal Prosecution." The key issue for us in these guidelines - and it's on page 12 in e-court - the Supreme Military Prosecutor's Office --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I was asking you a question concerning the Supreme Military Prosecutor's Office attached to the Main Staff, and I said it was the equivalent of -- or the counterpart of the Republic Prosecutor's Office on the civilian level, but your answer wasn't recorded. Could you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me show you page 12 of this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, when you reach a convenient point, we would take the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, because of the technical problem we are obviously experiencing, it would be a convenient point, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: While the witness is being escorted back to the stand, I note for the record that we sit for this final session today under Rule 15 bis, Judge Delvoie being absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us continue, Mr. Kovacevic. This document is "Guidelines for Identifying Criteria for Criminal Prosecution," issued by the Military Prosecutor's Office of the Main Staff of the armed forces in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 23 in Serbian and page 7 in English, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It will come up in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 23 in Serbian and page 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let's wait for the English. There it is. You see, here in these guidelines the Military Prosecutor's Office at the Main Staff of the army is issuing guidelines for crimes against humanity and international law pursuant to chapter 16 of the Criminal Code, and these guidelines are issued to subordinate military prosecutors' offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to page 25, and the English page is still 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So the Supreme Military Prosecutor's Office explains and guides the subordinate military prosecutors' offices on how they should work. It says: "The Criminal Code applicable on the territory of Republika Srpska defines 16 criminal offences, including genocide, Article 141; war crimes against the civilian population, Article 142; the wounded and the sick, prisoners of war," et cetera. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 33. That's page 9 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The Military Prosecutor's Office, in this part of the document, prescribes specific steps that military security organs and the military police must take to investigate and prosecute these crimes. And look at paragraph 4: "The organs of the military police and security and the military judicial authorities will grant priority to these crimes in their work so that the Main Staff and the other competent institutions should be informed as soon as possible so that they take steps in their own jurisdiction." Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This indubitably confirms what we just discussed, that these crimes from chapter 16, crimes against humanity and international law, fell within the exclusive purview of military judicial authorities. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I tender this document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure if this is maybe a bar table motion. I mean, this witness is not a member of the Military Prosecutor's Office, wasn't back in 1992. It's doubtful that he ever saw these guidelines. And do I not -- we do not agree with the Defence's representation that that's what this document says, that all war crimes are within the jurisdiction of the Military Prosecutor's Office. It doesn't say that. Or at least he hasn't pointed to any provision in it that does say that. But mainly this is not the witness to admit a document from the Military Prosecutor's Offices or the military court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Could we consider it becoming a part of the law library?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: I think it would be a very extended interpretation of a law library because this is not a law. I'm not sure what other things we have in the law library.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: The law library, as I understand it, is supposed to include all legislative or normative instruments that have been adopted by the authorities, and this would seem to fall under that category, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Well, it's not normative. It's guidelines. At least the way I interpret guidelines are they're there to guide someone, but they're not necessarily the law itself or a regulation itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, it seems that the -- this is not the witness through whom this should be exhibited. For the sake of simplicity, we will mark it for identification. The point that -- the exchange that Judge Harhoff just had with Mr. Olmsted, perhaps we can revisit the matter of the law library, because your experience would -- when I say your experience, I mean the common experience of the Bench and yourselves would have been that there are a number of matters of this similar nature which arguably could have been a part of the law library but have been treated differently. So at this point we just mark this for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand and appreciate, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D368 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, during the break I found that there -- there appears to be a problem with the -- with the e-court. A part of the document which is 1D04-2318 has not been uploaded in the e-court, and we don't have the translation to it. Now, this -- this part, these three pages I'm referring to are especially relevant for this case because they refer to the -- to the incidents which are listed in our indictment. So what I propose to do is that I show this to the -- to the witness, that we read so that it can be translated, and then after that I -- I will upload the -- we will upload the document in the e-court. If that is -- we can put it on the ELMO and -- and the witness can read from it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm really sorry for this situation, but for some reason I guess these things happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a document which is, in fact, a monthly report from the military organs at the command of the 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Just for clarification, while he's setting that up, I can access this through e-court. At least I've pulled it up. I'm not sure if it's the document you're referring to, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But the ERN is 0206-7965.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Oh, it's -- so -- I see. I understand now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So if we can -- if we can see the whole page first, please. We need the whole page. And the actual headline, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if you're able to read it. "A review of cases under action taken due to offences against humanity and international law."

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to read, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you see this highlighted passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... highlighted in yellow. If it can be brought up.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think you can see it better now. It says: "Since the beginning of 1993 to date, for the crime -- for the war crime against civilian population pursuant to Article 142 from the Criminal Code originally of the SFRY, proceedings have been instituted against: "1. Goran Amidzic, 2nd lieutenant in the VRS, Prosecutorial case VTK 375/93." Isn't that a military prosecution's number?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had this acronym VTK, V standing for "vojno," "military." Our number was TK.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then it says: "The request to start an investigation was filed on 8 March 1993 on the basis of a well-grounded suspicion that on the 1st of June, 1992, in Velagici village, municipality of Kljuc, they detained a group of about 80 civilians of Muslim ethnicity in the school building and that around 2130 hours there occurred a conflict caused by the detained civilians after which, in the ensuing commotion, the suspects opened fire from the weapons they had in their possession and killed all the persons who emerged from the school building. Investigation is ongoing." Have you heard about these killings in Velagici, in the school building?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of an incident like that. I don't know exactly where that place is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Kljuc municipality.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Kljuc, Sanski Most, somewhere there. I heard that an incident of those proportions had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can we see the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is page 2 of the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If we can highlight the part which -- the highlighted part, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Other crimes are listed on this page, and para 3 says: "Proceedings are instituted also against Zeljko Despot, Brace Maric, Drasko Lakic, Dragan Lakic, all of them soldiers of the VRS, Prosecution's file VTK 858/93, on the reasonable suspicion that in the night between the 7 and 8 August 1992, in Donje Sjenica village, Botonjici hamlet, they killed 12 civilians of Muslim ethnicity in the following way: In that night, they separated the women and children and transferred them across the River Sanica into Crnalici village, whereas 12 other persons were separated, killed, and then incinerated to hide the traces of the crime." And then it says: "The case has not been taken into action. No criminal proceedings have been instituted." I suppose this means that the initial document has not been written.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I suppose it's the request to submit an investigation, to start proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact, isn't it, that this case is registered as VTK 858/93, which indicates that the criminal complaint had been received, and the prosecutor's office is beginning to work on this case.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the prosecutor's number for that file.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can we see the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, on the last page, you see the signature of the military prosecutor, Captain Srboljub Jovicinac?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You know he was a military prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he succeeded Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That means that he was with the prosecutor's -- Military Prosecutor's Office at the command of the 1st Krajina Corps after Mr. Pisarevic left.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm -- now I'm not sure what to do with this. Shall we -- shall we reserve the number perhaps, and after I -- after I upload it in e-court that we get this number? Otherwise -- or just keep it on the record like -- like it was, and then after we upload it, we will show it to another witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm pretty sure we've been faced with this problem before. Can you remind me as to how we've dealt with it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't -- I don't think, Your Honours, that we had a similar problem like this one before. That is -- that is the reason why I'm so confused what to do else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Perhaps the simpler course so that we don't lose it in the system is to MFI it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was just notified -- I was just notified by my assistant that it's -- that this document is getting uploaded as 1D04-2869. It's going to be uploaded in e-court in any minute now. So if we can have the number then, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D369, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I should like to show you one more document. This is the Military Prosecutor's Office at the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D04-2403, tab 4. This is a report on crime incidents for 1992 and crime trends made in 1993, February 1993. I'd like page 4 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And I would only like you to give me one comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Could we have an English version of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm pretty sure that all the documents which we have are translated and uploaded, the English version as well. 1D04-2403; that's the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We cannot find a translation up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry. Then we will upload the translation. Just a short comment by the witness, and I will read.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 3, sub-heading: "Crimes Falling Under International Law of Warfare." It reads: "For this group of crimes in the reporting period, 21 criminal complaints have been filed against 43 persons, including 42 civilians and 1 officer." It's a fact, isn't it, that military prosecutor's offices had jurisdiction over these crimes rather than civilian --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: They had jurisdiction concerning these crimes even when a civilian was involved.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It follows from this document that they were qualified and had jurisdiction to act.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For the record, I said military prosecutor's offices, in the case of crimes like this, had jurisdiction even when perpetrators were not military personnel but civilians.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It says so in the document, because the indictment is against 42 civilians and 1 officer.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm informed that the CLSS translation is pending for this document. I don't know if there is an objection for admittance of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: We'd object to admit it through this witness. For one thing, we don't even know what this document is, but putting that aside, I presume it's a military document again, and this witness cannot really add to our understanding of this document. In addition, from what I've heard been read out, it is not even contradictory to the position the Prosecution is taking with regard to this very issue. It just simply is just reporting on a couple particular cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But in any event, inasmuch as our practice is when a document has not yet been translated to only mark it for identification, we would do that and Mr. Olmsted, when he would have had an opportunity to digest the document in its entirety, might find he has no objection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D370, Your Honours, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I have a few documents that you should be familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 1D00-2237, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a record of the on-site investigation made by the basic court in Banja Luka, and the number is KRI 546/92. It concerns a killing of a child, Suljo Culum, unfortunately. That was committed on the night between the 9th and the 10th of September, 1992, in the village of Bastasi. So this is a record of an on-site investigation signed by Investigating Judge Jevto Jankovic. Do you maybe recall this case, the murder of Suljo Culum?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I can see that Nebojsa Pantic, the public prosecutor, was present there. Not you but somebody else was present from the public prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I assume that then he was in charge of this case if he was present at the on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That doesn't necessarily follow. The usual practice was for the prosecutor to cover as many cases as possible of on-site investigations. And then the case file would be forwarded to one of the deputies who then processed it, because the deputies did other work, too, and did not have either the time or the ability to actually attend the on-site investigations. And this is why the boss, the public prosecutor, actually did that job upon receiving notice from the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, since you're not familiar with this case, we're for the going to pursue it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 2D00-2091, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, this document that we've just discussed, the one that's still on the screen, it is clear that this minor, Suljo Culum, is a member of the Muslim ethnic community?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, based on his first and last name, it's quite apparent.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could we please look at 1D00-2091.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a criminal report filed to the basic public prosecutor's office by the Banja Luka Public Security Station. The date is the 15th of September, 1992. It is the crime of causing danger, public danger, under Article 172, and the injured party is Kadro Vehabovic from Tehija Street, number 42, in Banja Luka. We could conclude on the basis of his name, Kadro Vehabovic, that this is a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you maybe know something about this case? A barn and haystack were set on fire, and the damage was quite bad.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I seem to remember it, but somewhat unclearly. I remember it because the -- it -- the damage was quite severe.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps if we show you the page 2 of this record of the on-site investigation, then perhaps ... The on-site investigation was carried out on the 9th of September, 1992, but as far as I can see, authorised officials of the Banja Luka Security Services Centre visited the scene, so the investigating judge and the public prosecutor were not present on site, and they conducted the on-site investigation pursuant to an authorisation given to them by the investigating judge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. Well, they were supposed to get the authorisation, and I assume that they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please look at page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this is the 9th of September, 1992, the record of the on-site investigation. You can see that it's signed by the authorised official from the public security station in Banja Luka -- or, rather, the CSB, the security services centre, because I can see it was -- the criminal report was signed by Stojan Zupljanin, the chief. And this is all about -- and, actually, the signature of the authorised official shows us that this is Zijad Hadziselimovic. Do you know this man, an official from the security services centre?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know his name, but I do know that he worked in the police. I didn't work with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hadziselimovic is a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, based on his name, I can conclude that t.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in September 1992, he worked in the Banja Luka Security Services Centre; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, apparently.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Unless there are any objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, for what purpose and on what basis? This witness said at most he has a vague recollection of the case and has really not added anything to what the document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I can give my explanation, but if that is okay with the -- with my friend from the Prosecutor that I do that in front of the witness, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And I suppose the nexus that you find Mr. Zecevic is that this was signed by Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, among other things, yes, Your Honours, and maybe there is -- there is some misunderstanding from my part of the case of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: No, there's -- well, I can't say that definitively that there's no understanding -- complete understanding of your case, but my objection is that this is not the witness to admit this kind of document through, since he knows nothing about the -- about the case and has never seen this document before. And are we going to go through this exercise where we're going to show him a bunch of criminal reports he knows nothing about and then admit them into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, with all due respect, you don't expect the prosecutor to remember, after 18 years, each and every case. I'm showing him -- I'm showing him a criminal complaint which was obviously received in the Office of the Prosecutor where this witness was working. He vaguely remembers this -- this incident, and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, it appears to me that the document is ex facie relevant, and for the sake of simplicity, I think it should be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D371, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to show you another case, 1D00-1951. Again, it's a criminal report submitted to the basic public prosecutor's office in Banja Luka, signed by the centre chief, Mr. Zupljanin, although, interestingly, I don't see this noted on the translation. But we can all see that there is -- there are the words "Centre Chief Stojan Zupljanin" on the original.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Again, this is a criminal report filed to your public prosecutor's office, the one where you worked. Oh, I do apologise. I can see that at page 2 there is an indication that there is a signature on the original. So this is a criminal report. The crime is causing a public danger. And the injured party is Husref Smajlagic From Banja Luka. Are you familiar with this case?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this case, but I do know the name. I think that this was a man who served as the secretary in the basic court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the record - and I'll show you page 2, that's 1st of September, 1992, Husein Smajlagic is a Muslim; right?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, based on his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you can see here the on-site investigation report, paragraph 2, Husein Smajlagic, judge of this court?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you remember that he was a judge?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I remember that he -- I remember him and this document. It was of some interest because in his previous term he was a secretary and -- the secretary and then he was appointed a judge. I know that there was some debate, but at any rate he was an officer of the court and yet this happened to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And this was signed by Investigating Judge Djordje Stojakovic. Do you remember that judge?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The event occurred on the 24th of June, 1992. There is a photo file attached. And probably the criminal report was filed in September after the forensic investigation had been carried out.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So you know the injured party in this case; he was a judge of the basic court in Banja Luka; the criminal report was filed in September 1992; the incident occurred in June 1992; and you do not recall the case, do you?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I know stories about the incident because he was a judge. Well, a long time has passed, but I know that we discussed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You did not act in this case as a public prosecutor, but you know that this case existed?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. I know in -- in my capacity as the resident of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And at any rate he was a colleague of yours?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document also.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: The speakers are kindly asked not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, in anticipation of the objection that Mr. Olmsted is likely to make, how many more of these documents do you intend to tender to illustrate your point, because I assume that that is your purpose. They're illustrative of what was going on in terms of -- of cases of this nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is correct, Your Honour, and I have two more cases, two more examples of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D372, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to look at 1D00-1939.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a criminal report, again signed by centre chief Mr. Stojan Zupljanin. The date is the 1st of September, 1992. It's a crime, causing public danger, committed against Emir Nezirevic from Banja Luka, and we his address. Based on his name, I would say that Emir Nezirevic is a Muslim; right?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I've decided to use this case as a typical case because here fire was set to a van, a Volkswagen van, but the fire was set when the perpetrator fired a rifle-launched grenade on the vehicle, which caused the fire. Are you familiar with this case? Do you remember it at all?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't be certain. I'm -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what a rifle-launched grenade is?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. I know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a highly destructive explosive device, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's highly destructive.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it does illustrate -- its illustrative. This incident happened on the 26 of August, 1992, and it shows us what the security situation was like in the area of Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. I actually did speak about that myself in my evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like us to mark this document for identification unless there are any objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D373, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And finally, 1D00-1929. 1929.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you can see this is a criminal report, again, signed by the chief of the security services centre, Stojan Zupljanin. The date is the 31st of August, 1992. It was submitted to the public prosecutor's office where you yourself worked. Again, it's the crime of causing public danger, and the injured party is Rifat Secic. Again, it's a Muslim, is he not?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Based on his name, I can conclude that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this describes an event in the night between the 15th and the 16th of June, 1992, when fire was set to his weekend house, to the weekend house owned by Rifat Secic. Is it true?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We see the on-site investigation report, the Official Note. Do you perhaps remember this case?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I like to have this document marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D374, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to look at 1D23 -- that's MFI. This is the criminal case file 1D203 MFI. This is a report on the arrest -- arrest and remand in custody. The date is the 17th of April, 1992. It is signed by the centre chief, Stojan Zupljanin. And I will show you page 2, which is the criminal report. You can see that a criminal report was filed against Damir Halilovic. The crime is murder. Damir Halilovic is a Muslim, is he not?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the criminal report is filed because there are grounds to suspect that he committed murder under Article 36, paragraph (1), of the Criminal Code, and the description of the crime is that on the afternoon of 15 April 1992, he killed, in the Bujrum restaurant, Enis Krkic. He shot him. And based on Enis Krkic's name, we can also conclude that he's a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this case?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me show you another document from September 1992. You might be familiar with the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 1D01-0024.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know Vinko Djurdjic, a judge of the court in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, know him his name -- I know him by name only.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: He's a judge who dealt with criminal cases?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From 1992 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a report on the forensic analysis of firearms and bullet casings in connection with the murders of Adnan Kobasic, Zahid Mahic; so both would be Muslims. And police officers Zivko Vrhovac, Miodrag Kovacevic, and Miloje Maljkovic, carried out on the 23rd and the 24th of September, 1992, in Banja Luka. Since, in addition to two Muslims, we have three police officers who were victims, I assume that you can recall this event.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall this incident. I don't know whether I dealt with it, but I -- I do remember that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was quite striking.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown page 4 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were there proceedings before court regarding this crime?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't recall. I assume that proceedings were conducted, because it was an interesting case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You can see here that the forensic analysis, the ballistic analysis, was carried out by Vilko Maric.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember him. He was our expert. And he went on being an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And senior inspector Srdjan Oljaca in the security services centre in Banja Luka, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D375, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just to illustrate the point, I would like to show you document 1D00-1998. You see the cover letter from the public security station in Banja Luka, signed by Zoran Josic, department chief. And he is hereby submitting to the public prosecutor's office the record of a verbal -- of the receipt of a verbal criminal report submitted by Ejub Pasalic against unknown perpetrators for causing public danger.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You are familiar with this kind of form? I'm sure that you received many such records of verbal criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this kind of form, and it is true that we did receive quite a few of those reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the injured party here is a member of the Muslim ethnicity, Ejub Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In light of the situation that you described for us and the incidents that occurred such as this one which we said was quite illustrative, where a car was hit by a rifle-launched grenade, there were quite a few or there -- there was a substantial number of criminal reports where perpetrators were unidentified. Is it not the case?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Based on your experience as a prosecutor, even in peacetime, in a normal situation, if we may call it that, a certain percentage, a high percentage, at least initially, of criminal reports are filed against unidentified perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then after a while, the perpetrators of crime are identified and then the case became -- becomes active again when this person is arrested?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The report is filed that the perpetrator of a crime has been identified, and then, if necessary, this person is arrested and remanded in custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Of course, there are situations where the police is able to identify the perpetrator but the perpetrator is not in the territory covered by the municipality or the location where the crime was committed but might be temporarily working abroad or something like that. There were such cases; right?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in cases like that, nothing is done until the person is arrested, and at times it can take several years for this person to be arrested and extradited to the country where he committed the crime?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I'm familiar with this practice. I know of cases such as this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So it is a characteristic feature of the prosecutor's work and police work that initially there is a large number of crimes for which perpetrators are unknown?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And when you have a situation such as this one, the one you've just described for us in the territory of Banja Luka, with a huge influx of refugees, constant passage of military columns, the reservists, and general chaos, then one should not wonder at the fact that the number of cases with unidentified perpetrators should be on the rise?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, unless there are any objections, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I thought that you only wanted to show this document for illustration. It's it forwarding letter, and I fail to see the relevance, quite frankly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we had, previously, a witness who was commenting on the KU registers, if you remember, and we were talking about the oral -- the possibility of filing oral criminal complaints. Just for the purposes of establishing that from the -- from the characteristic document, I wanted to introduce this document. There is no other purpose for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OLMSTED
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's been established through the other witness that there were oral reports, and he -- the evidence was that this would have been filed as a criminal report with the Office of the Prosecutor because it involves a serious crime. And I think this witness hasn't really gone beyond that in explaining this particular document any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I don't see how it advances the matter any, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. [Interpretation] I would like the witness to look at 1D199 MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you if you are familiar with this case. That's a criminal -- or, rather, it's the decision to remand seven persons in custody, all ethnic Serbs, signed by centre chief Stojan Zupljanin. The date is the 3rd of July, 1992. It's a group that committed 37 crimes, robberies, murder, racketeering, causing public danger, and so on; and among other crimes, they also set explosives that destroyed business premises and killed Mustafa Smajlagic from Banja Luka. Mustafa Smajlagic is a Muslim; right?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And perhaps I can show page 2 to you so that we can see the names of these persons. It's Dragan Jovorac, aka Java; Mladen Josic; Goran Banjac; Jelenko Sjenica; Dragan Milasinovic. They were prosecuted, right, for these crimes, 37 of them, in the area of Banja Luka? A large number of crimes; right?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. They were known, as perpetrators. Most of these people were known criminals.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And from this decision we see that in keeping with the law, and the person who has signed this is Stojan Zupljanin, they were remanded in custody for up to 72 hours.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 3rd of July, and this document submitted to you, the basic prosecutor's office, bears the date 6th of July. That's all done within the first 72 hours exactly in conformity with the law.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the prescribed time-frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the witness recognised this group and knows that this procedure took place, I suggest that we give this document a proper number, that it be taken off the MFI list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked. Well, de-MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. [Interpretation] 1D206 MFI is the next document I would need.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you are aware of this incident dated 18 June. It's a report on arrest and hand-over, signed by Stojan Zupljanin. The accused is Dragoslav Kuzmic, and the charge is aiding and abetting the crime of murder. And the victim is Mustafa Smajlagic from Banja Luka, and it all happened in Banja Luka. Smajlagic, Mustafa; that's a Muslim name?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the perpetrator, Dragoslav Kuzmic, sounds like a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I see from the minutes that the deputy of the public prosecutor was there, Mrs. Marjanac?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember she was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But you don't remember this incident?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: One more document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D01-0123, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you see this? This cover page is the cover of the file, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In practice, every case had its own case file, both in the prosecutor's office and the police?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And, finally, in the court?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You see, this is the case file, Milan Stankovic, Article 36. The injured party is Ante Jurkic; I suppose that's a Croat?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the name and surname, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Date: 18 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is typical and indicative because it's one of the rare files that are complete, and in practice, always, on the inside of the cover page, a list was made of all the documents contained in the file. And then it goes number by number -- your answer was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And as new documents were added, they were added to the list, given a number, the title of the document was written in, and it was placed in the file. That was general practice in the police, in the prosecutor's offices, and in courts?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was prescribed common practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is this the same criminal report filed by the CSB where Stojan Zupljanin was chief? Are you familiar with this murder of Ante Jurkovic? Do you know about Milan Stankovic?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've never heard of that man.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question, sir. You worked in the prosecutor's office until what time in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Until what time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until the end of 1989.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then if I understood correctly, you started working in some business?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in 1992, you returned to the prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since you were involved in business, you're probably aware of how the economic situation evolved from 1989 until the outbreak of the conflict in 1992? Many enterprises went into ground?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What I mean is that they went bankrupt. They were unable to operate any more.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And one business that I had with a colleague faced the same fate. We had no money to operate any more, and we started bankruptcy proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no market developed enough to enable us to continue working as we had worked before. We were just condemned to bankruptcy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that's why you returned to the prosecutor's office. You were out of work, no money to live on.

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's one of the reasons why I returned to the prosecutor's office, to support my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But it's a fact, is isn't it, that this situation was general and widespread, and there is almost no person who was untouched by it? There was general joblessness, businesses closing down, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: MARINKO KOVACEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. And we have conveniently come to the end of today's sitting. Mr. Krgovic, I assume that you will begin your cross-examination when we resume on Monday. Mr. Kovacevic, we are about to rise for the day, and we will resume on Monday morning. I remind you of what I told you yesterday, that you cannot discuss your testimony with anyone outside the court nor have communication with counsel until you're released as a witness. So we take the adjournment. I wish everyone a safe weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 6th day of September, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.44 p.m.,
